clue.text: Opening word of cryptic message not good

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the letters left are jumbled
not tells us to leave out the abbreviation that follows from the word before

explanation.surface: A secret message's first word turns out to be a poor one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' takes G from MESSAGE, leaving MESSAE, and 'cryptic' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, 'Open sesame' is the magic phrase that opens the robbers' cave.

clue.text: Wine container

definitions.meaning: an old name for a dry white wine from Spain or the Canaries
a large bag of coarse cloth for holding goods

explanation.definitionFit: Two separate senses: a sherry-like fortified wine of Shakespeare's day, and a coarse cloth bag.

clue.text: Dine without fish in the revolution

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dining word goes round the fish

parts.note: to sup is to eat an evening meal
hake is a sea fish related to cod

explanation.surface: A diner refuses fish while some uprising goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the dining word wraps round the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A drastic reorganisation of an organisation is a thorough upheaval, loosely a revolution.

clue.text: Deer English attempt to get with small arms fire

parts.note: the musk deer is a small Asian deer, so musk can stand for deer
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A deer-hunting Englishman tries his luck with a rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketry is the firing of muskets or rifles, collectively the fire of light weapons.

clue.text: Romany almost turns on girl with a telescope

indicators.note: turns tells us to read the shortened word backwards
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a Romany is a gypsy
lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A traveller turns to watch a young woman through a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GYPSY to GYPS and 'turns' reverses that to SPYG, which goes on LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, as carried by sailors.

clue.text: Old school gets Chico plenty confused!

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chico, one of the Marx Brothers, is baffled by an old-fashioned college.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain polytechnics were colleges of higher education that became universities in 1992, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British polytechnic was a former type of college for higher education, now defunct.

clue.text: Chuck takes young lady round in many countries

indicators.note: round means the word for young lady encircles the throwing word

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a young woman
to chuck is to throw, and to lob is to throw high

explanation.surface: Chuck takes his girlfriend on a trip around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something global is worldwide, happening across lots of nations at once.

clue.text: A parent with vitality — that's fabulous!

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
zing means energy or liveliness

explanation.surface: A lively mother is described as wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing and fabulous are both informal words of high praise meaning wonderful.

clue.text: Old nurse caught naughty miscreant

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An elderly nurse is caught being badly behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a synonym for a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Sheriff starts in pursuit — it's a bit of a dance

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letter goes inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a pursuit is a chase

indicators.note: starts means we take just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sheriff gives chase in a scene that is a bit of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasse is a gliding step in ballroom dancing, so only one part of a dance.

clue.text: The Spanish manage without Miss Spenlow, where wealth is thought to be had

definitions.text: where wealth is thought to be had

indicators.note: without in the sense of outside, placing the managing word beyond the name

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
Dora Spenlow is David Copperfield's child-bride in the Dickens novel
to do is to manage, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: Spaniards cope without a Dickens heroine in a place of fabled riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Dora Spenlow is the first wife of David Copperfield in Dickens's novel. 'without' means outside, here simply after the name.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the fabled city of gold sought by Spanish explorers in South America.

clue.text: Limited resource feeds ten somehow before chucking out

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ration is a fixed, limited allowance of something scarce

explanation.surface: Scarce supplies feed ten people before some are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited resource' sits first in the clue but its piece ends the answer; 'somehow' shuffles only the two middle words into DEFENEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenestration is the act of throwing someone out of a window, a specific kind of ejection.

clue.text: Cough up and look forward to speak

parts.note: to expect is to look forward to something
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone clears their throat in anticipation of making a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to bring up phlegm from the chest by coughing.

clue.text: A great deal of nothing?

parts.note: a great deal of empty space read as 'hyper' (excessive) plus 'space', the science-fiction region beyond normal space

explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction a dimension beyond ordinary space, playfully a huge expanse of emptiness.

clue.text: Far from 21, like party policies?

definitions.meaning: far from being charred, i.e. underdone, only partly cooked
describes political plans that are poorly thought out

explanation.definitionFit: Partly cooked bread is far from charred; figuratively the phrase means ill-conceived plans.

clue.text: Character of Borodin and Stravinsky

definitions.meaning: Prince ... is the title role in Borodin's opera
the composer's first name, standing for the man himself

explanation.definitionFit: The name of Borodin's opera hero and the Christian name of the Russian composer Stravinsky.

clue.text: In a walk, girl is willing to be led

indicators.note: in tells us the girl's name is placed inside the walking word

parts.note: an amble is a leisurely walk
Ena is a girl's name, common in crosswords

explanation.surface: A girl strolling along is happy to be guided.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means open to persuasion or easily guided, so docile.

clue.text: Go on endlessly about not being decent

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the shortened word round
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to dwell is to go on at length about a subject

explanation.surface: Someone keeps harping on about indecency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts DWELL to DWEL and 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd describes crude, indecent behaviour or talk, so lacking decency.

clue.text: Following hostilities, rebel elements out east get bird

indicators.note: following tells us the rearranged letters come after the fighting word

parts.note: hostilities means war

indicators.note: elements suggests the word broken into parts and reassembled
out tells us to remove the compass letter from the word

explanation.surface: After the fighting, rebel fighters in the east are out to get a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out east' drops one E from REBEL and 'elements' rearranges the remaining RBEL as BLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Warblers are a family of small songbirds.

clue.text: Mean euphemistically a lone comic turn

indicators.note: a turn is a performance and also a twist, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary comedian performs a stand-up spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like a comedian's act, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical is a polite way of calling someone stingy, saying careful with money.

clue.text: Shiny element surrounding Ibsen character in Somerset

indicators.note: surrounding means the chemical symbol goes around the character

parts.note: chromium, used for shiny plating, has symbol Cr
Hedda Gabler is the title role in Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: A gleaming metal encircles an Ibsen heroine in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEDDAR is a village in Somerset, a county in south-west England, famous for its gorge and cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a village located in that English county, home of the cheese.

clue.text: Mark time in classic character

indicators.note: in tells us the time abbreviation goes inside the Greek letter

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the classical Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A note of time is marked in an old Greek script.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or a visible spot on the skin.

clue.text: Made bread turn into carbon perhaps?

definitions.text: Made bread turn into carbon perhaps?

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned or reworked, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Someone has left the toast under the grill until it is charred.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranged letters describe toast reduced to carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcooked bread becomes charcoal-like, which is the phrase's literal sense.

clue.text: Knot turns foul

indicators.note: turns means the word for foul is read backwards

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A knot goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarl in a tree trunk or piece of wood.

clue.text: Weight of Kipling's work about record with soldiers

indicators.note: about tells us the novel's title goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Kim is Kipling's novel of India
a log is a record, as in a ship's log
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Kipling's work about soldiers seems heavy going.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilogram is the standard metric unit of mass, a thousand grams.

clue.text: Scot ill in African city

indicators.note: in tells us the word for ill goes inside the Scottish name

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name
bad means unwell, as in feeling bad

explanation.surface: A Scotsman falls ill in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-west Nigeria.

clue.text: The Times displaying lack of enlightenment?

definitions.text: The Times displaying lack of enlightenment?

parts.words: The Times displaying lack of enlightenment?
parts.note: not the newspaper but a historical period thought of as unenlightened

explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval period in Europe, regarded as lacking learning and culture.

clue.text: Object of Bush's war — a bit of tactical blunder

indicators.note: a bit of means only a small part, here the opening letter, is taken

parts.note: a blunder is an error

explanation.surface: A tactical mistake in George W. Bush's campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Bush declared a war on terror after the September 2001 attacks.
